title: Chess, But I Can LAUNCH My Pawns
summary: Angry-Birds / penguin-push style chess vs Stockfish. As his move the player can click a slingshot icon, drag back on one of his pawns and launch it with chosen direction and power; the pawn slides physically across the board, colliding with and knocking enemy pieces off the board (pushed-off pieces are removed), then all pieces snap to the nearest squares. Kings are never affected by the bumping. Overshooting can send your own pawn off the board. After an early queen knockout, the narrator restricts himself to winning with pawns only and finishes with a launched-pawn promotion ladder mate.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600).
On his turn the player may either make a normal move or launch one pawn: drag back from the pawn (slingshot) to set direction and power, release.
The launched pawn travels with physics (sliding, collisions); enemy pieces it hits are pushed and any piece pushed off the board edge is removed; the pawn itself can fly off the board if overpowered.
After the launch resolves, all pieces snap back to the nearest board squares (pawn often ends a square or more forward).
Kings are immune to bumping (can't be knocked off).
A pawn that ends on the 8th rank promotes (e.g. g8 for ladder mate).
win_condition: Checkmate Stockfish (normal checkmate; kings can't be bumped off).
